content: Iron rusts from disuse; stagnant water loses its purity; even so does inaction sap the vigor of the mind.
author: Leonardo da Vinci
sourceWork: Leonardo da Vinci's Essays & Philosophical Writings
story:
Preserved as part of Leonardo da Vinci's enduring intellectual legacy, this reflection addresses the fundamental nature of action and creativity. Across his life and work, Leonardo da Vinci returned repeatedly to the conviction that personal integrity, honest observation, and clarity of purpose are the foundational pillars of a life well-lived.

Contemplating this truth invites us to step back from the frantic rush of daily demands. By examining our assumptions with fresh eyes, we discover the inner grounding necessary to act with wisdom and quiet conviction.
reflectionPrompt: How can you welcome mistakes and awkward beginnings as essential steps in your creative evolution?
